subject: ela
intro: Eleventh graders cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of an informational text, including determining where the text leaves matters uncertain. Advanced readers notice when a text acknowledges its own limits or open questions.

items.prompt:
Read.

The study found a strong link between the drug and recovery, but the authors note the sample was small and call for further research.

Where does the text leave a matter UNCERTAIN?

steps: The authors flag the small sample and call for more study.
So the strength of the link remains uncertain pending further research.
solution.answer: Whether the link truly holds remains uncertain, given the small sample.

items.prompt:
Read.

After the law passed, crime fell, but so did the national crime rate overall.

What does the evidence leave uncertain?

steps: Crime fell everywhere, so the law may not be the cause.
So whether the law itself caused the local drop is uncertain.
solution.answer: Whether the law caused the drop, since crime fell nationally too.

items.prompt: Why do credible texts sometimes flag UNCERTAINTY?

steps: Acknowledging limits is honest and accurate.
So it makes the text more credible and precise.
solution.answer: It makes the text more credible and precise.

items.prompt: When a text flags what is not yet known, it marks ____.
The most convincing proof is the ____ evidence.
An inference is a conclusion drawn from ____.
